American scouts took a cataclysmic nose dive in the 1970s when they de-emphasized outdoor survival skills. A big push for the creation of scouts in the first place was the comedown from WW1 and the ramp-up into WW2 (likely the same reasoning for scouting in Europe you experienced). People realized that training needed to start sooner for potential conflicts.

But when the 1970s rolled around it became a lot more 'suburban'/community volunteer friendly (aka don't do drugs, spy on your neighbors, bake cookies/shit), BSA lost something like ~2 million members because of that change. It's not really recovered since then and its suffered under poor management and decision making for decades. The U.S. pop is higher than ever but scout membership is lower than it was during the terrible 1970s change.

Co-ed isn't a big deal since there will be girl troops and boy troops, they'll all just be all under the same umbrella organization now.
